source_support_reviews.actual_text: Ongunnon, began, takes the three infinitives onwinnan, attack, niman, take, and hęrgian, plunder. Pihtas are the Picts, Scottas the Scots; norðan and westan mean from the north and from the west. Hīe refers to the Britons introduced in the separate context; ǣhta means possessions.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Iermdon and hīendon mean afflicted and oppressed. Fela gēara means for many years, with genitive after fela. Hīe can be the Britons as object with the raiders continuing as subject, or the raiders as subject with a Briton object understood; the events do not change. Do not infer a unique case from the spelling.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: On ðǣre unstilnesse, amid that unrest. Onsęndon is the exact prefixed sent; the Britons are now the subject. Ǣrendwrecan, messengers; tō Rome, to Rome. Mid gewritum and wēpendre bēne means with letters and a tearful petition. Wēpendre is a present participle, strong dative feminine singular agreeing with bēne.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: In him fultumes bǣdon, him names the Romans asked and fultumes is the genitive thing requested: help. Hīernes is obedience; singāl is continual; underðēodnes is subjection. Ēaðmōde and singāle are accusative feminine singular. The promise is made by the Britons to the Romans.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Gefultumoden is a preterite subjunctive: if they, the Romans, would help them, the Britons. The following ðæt clause gives the purpose, so that they might overcome their enemies. Meahten is the known preterite subjunctive plural of magan; oferwinnan means overcome. This whole reported condition/purpose sequence is supported locally.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Here the subject of onsęndon is the Romans, while him refers to the Britons. Tō fultume means as help/to their aid. The Old English says they sent an army in the active voice; Cook compares a passive Latin expression. Preserve the actual Old English voice when analyzing it.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Sōna ðæs-ðe means as soon as. On ðis īgland has the accusative goal, to/onto this island. Hīe refers to the Roman force. The following ðā resumes the narrative.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Campedon, fought; wið hiera fēondum, against their enemies, with the source dative after wið. Him micel wæl ongeslōgon means inflicted great slaughter on them. Of hiera gemǣrum means out of their borders, with dative after of; the borders belong to the Britons, Rome’s allies. Āflīemdon means put to flight, reinforcing ādrifon. The enemy object carries on through the coordinated verbs.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Lǣrdon means advised/instructed. Fæsten is a fortification; worhten is the known unprefixed wyrcean preterite subjunctive, here make/build in the advice clause. Him tō gebeorge means for their own protection. The Romans give the advice and the Britons are to build. The source’s wið + dative remains locally supplied.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Sige means victory. Mid micle sige is with great victory: the adjective has the instrumental micle beside the dative noun, as Cook’s note directs. Treat this as a supplied source construction. Hām is the directional home, without a preposition.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Read the three ðā forms in order as when, then, the. The first ðæt is an anticipatory object, this/that, expanded by the later that-clause. Ongēaton means realized; ǣrran gewinnan means former enemies. Gewinnan is a weak masculine plural noun, distinct from the previously supplied neuter gewinn, trouble.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Rōmanisca is the weak masculine adjective Roman. Wæs onweg gewiten means had gone away: gewiten is the past participle of intransitive gewītan. This is an intransitive completed-state/perfect expression, not a passive. The source has plain-e onweg; retain it beside the earlier selected onwęg.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: The returning subject is the Picts and Scots. Sōna means immediately; mid sciphęre, with a fleet. On hiera landgemǣru has accusative plural for movement into their territory; the territory is the Britons’.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Cwealdon means killed. Slōgon and cwealdon reinforce the attack. Ealle is all, naturally people in context; the following neuter ðæt is a headless/collective all that they encountered. A translation all they encountered need not pretend that ðæt is an overt masculine personal relative. Cook’s Latin note reads cædunt.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Swā-swā means just as/like. Rīpe ierðe means ripe crops, a collective feminine accusative phrase. Fortrǣdon, trampled down; fornōmon, destroyed/laid waste. The Britons are treated as a crop that is trampled; the object continues from the preceding clauses.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Foriermdon means ruined/reduced to misery. Hīe is the Britons as object. Mid ealle is the fixed phrase completely/utterly; ealle is instrumental here. The complete phrase is supplied.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Use the fixed phrase æt nīehstan, at length. Its ending is supplied; no general superlative system is required.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Use fēowertig gēara, forty years. This whole duration phrase is supplied; the higher numeral takes the genitive gēara. The duration construction is discussed in this unit.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Rōmane, Romans, is the supplied nominative plural; on Breotone, in Britain, supplies the place-name dative. Retain the preterite target.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Use nāh, does not own, for the negative possession clause. Cook’s hint sē ðe is retained as printed; the model may use the earlier selected Se ðe, he who. The long-vowel sē is a supplied source spelling, not a newly required paradigm.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Reuse the supplied contraction nis, is not, for the negative be-clause. This local form does not teach the full negative verb system.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Cook prints first (ǣrest). Treat this as a lexical hint: use the previously taught ordinal ǣresta and the needed agreeing form ǣrestan in ðone ǣrestan fisc. The uninflected printed hint is preserved in the prompt.
source_support_reviews.scope: Visible support, not a new unaided-recall milestone; actual task wording and required roles have been reviewed.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Twēntig means twenty. Use the supplied measure phrase twēntig fōta; the newly taught genitive of extent also governs seofon fōta.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Use the supplied nolde, the contracted negative preterite subjunctive singular of willan, in the reported later intention. Nǣfre mā adds never again; it combines with the negative finite verb. This one supplied contraction does not assign the entire negative paradigm.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Use the supplied nominative lēo, lion, after the second swā. No full paradigm of this loanword is assigned.

source_support_reviews.actual_text: Use on ōðre, into another, with feminine accusative singular ōðre and an understood ceastre, city. Cook prints (om. an)other: omit the article an, not the sense another. The city omission is supplied locally.

scope_checks.check: Only the actual Units1–11 contracts and cumulative registers establish prior teaching; supplied historical exposures are not production milestones.
All38 exact Cook items remain assigned and all38 original task IDs are keyed; no difficult item has disappeared into an unrecorded deferral.
Present and preterite inflection are distinguished from contextual future, anterior and ongoing reference; the material does not mechanically translate modern auxiliary words.
Twelve habban indicative construction positions are separate from692 inflectional cells. Finite subject agreement, accusative object role and selected bare past participle are all taught.
Object-agreeing participles are evidenced and accepted only where actual inflection and use are supported; no new unrestricted participial adjective declension or causative system is assigned.
Wesan+gewiten and wesan+sittende remain recognition constructions. Present-participle spelling alone does not assign an English progressive.

Reported simultaneous, anterior and intended later content is analyzed relative to the report. Syncretic hæfde/nolde forms are identified by target and context; subjunctive is not equated with falsity.
Agentless passive transformations intentionally omit the active agent. No new Old English fram-agent frame is demanded.
Ten complete indicative systems, nine command pairs, five participle pairs and two infinitive pairs are clearly bounded. No unassigned gemētan participle or free tō-infinitive production is inferred.
All22 noun systems and14 adjective systems have full literal or explicit model-derived routes. Abstract plural cells and adjective instrumental cells retain recognition reference scope.
Exact source forms and constructions remain visibly supplied: names, larger quantities, āgān/willan negatives, the city ellipse, source participial agreement and source-specific prepositional cases.
Quantitative mā, two separated equative swā roles, single nominal-comparison swā, predicative possession and beneficiary dative are explicitly supported beyond prior headword familiarity.
Lexical frames distinguish rich-in harvest, absolute seeing, objectless ceasing/failing, lethal striking, preparation, writing, sending, pursuing and leave-taking of a homeland.
The exact155-word source retains both paragraphs,21notes and22anchors. Historical ethnological speculation is labeled archival commentary and is not taught as a contemporary conclusion.

The new53-word connected account and all12 translated examples are declared new composition. Explicit completion contexts precede the relevant examples/tasks; all new text uses resolved vocabulary, forms and scope.
Cardinal ān remains one; neither witness additions nor idiomatic English a house promote an indefinite article.
